set.body:
Source: 2026-08-03 quality review. Mechanism traced in source; site behaviour NOT yet confirmed against a capture.

Problem:
Slurm names a heterogeneous job component `<leader>+<offset>`, for example 12345+0. SlurmJobIdentity.parse (SlurmParsers.scala:425-434) splits only on the last underscore, so it has no notion of `+`.

Traced consequence, and it is not a rejection:
- parse("12345+0") finds no underscore and returns Right("12345+0" -> None).
- JobId.from then ACCEPTS it, because IdentifierRules.text (kernel/Identifiers.scala:13-20) rejects only null, empty, over-length, whitespace and control characters. `+` passes.
- The observation therefore carries JobRef(JobId("12345+0"), None), while the bound attempt carries the leader id sbatch returned, JobRef(JobId("12345"), None).
- ControlTransition.recordObservations matches by exact JobRef through byJob.get, so the lookup misses and the attempt takes the not-reported path.

The attempt is then treated as unobserved rather than as a row the parser could not understand. That is the bad failure mode: a silent no-match produces "the scheduler did not report this job", which an operator reads as a scheduler or connectivity problem, instead of a diagnostic naming an unsupported id shape.

Reachability, unverified:
This library submits through sbatch, which returns a plain leader id, so a het component row appears only when the submitted script itself carries het-job directives such as `#SBATCH hetjob`. That is possible through the inline script path, so it is reachable by a user without any library support for het jobs. Whether it happens in practice at a real site is exactly what is unknown.

Blocked on evidence. Do not implement from the documented format alone; this needs captured squeue and sacct transcripts for a het job so the fixture pins what the surfaces actually emit for the leader, the components, and the accounting rows.

Acceptance once evidence exists:
- A het component row either resolves to the allocation the caller asked about, or produces a diagnostic naming the unsupported shape. It must not silently fail to match.
- Whichever is chosen, a fixture from a real capture pins it.
- Decide explicitly whether a het component is a distinct operational identity or a facet of the leader, and record the decision; that choice determines whether JobRef needs to represent the offset at all.
set.title: P8.G5: Heterogeneous job component ids are parsed into an id that never matches
